Eight controls:two-argument fresh creation and three-argument default-value update over the same coordinates/frames. Entire1680-byte maps and calculated bounds compared.

Exact C l_selection_setpoint and six selvar storage/bounds functions compile unchanged. Fixed typed Lua adapters implement only successful argc2/3/4 paths: selection validation, integer reads, stack pop/new/settop. The allocation adapter invokes real selection_new; full userdata/metatable allocation, Lua VM/parser and invalid-input diagnostics are not executed.

C coordinate adapter asserts explicit nonnegative inputs, ANY_LOC and null room, then adds the stated frame origin. It is not a general coordinate resolver. JS uses the real coordinate resolver on the production game state and frame established by public level_init/map; the exported production wrapper receives that frame and a null-room coder view.

This is a wrapper/API-boundary proof, not invocation through the private Lua-global symbol or a shipped loader. Source confirms the production Lua-global set method forwards args/env to this exact wrapper. No arbitrary Lua runtime or internal storage mutation is introduced.

Only absolute selection objects are supplied. Existing objects retain identity and an unrelated(35,17) anchor; fresh objects have only the new point. No relative-selection, mixed-frame, subroom, random-coordinate, zero/one-argument, out-of-bounds, invalid-input or error parity claim.

Values plus1 are1..127, representable with either signed or unsigned char. No compiler-dependent narrowing, embedded-NUL selection storage or larger numeric domain is tested. No RNG or runtime behavior claim.
The four scanner keys describe one delegated selection setter cause. Prior same-frame OR/sub proof, mixed-frame fixes, cave-cap unresolved lead and three parked gaps retain their own boundaries.
